themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,900% spike (z-score: 14.74)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or sudden enforcement gap in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 average weekly baseline (z-score: 14.74)
Most statistically anomalous spike in district data
Pattern broke dramatically in final week of observation window
reporting_angles: Ground canvass: what illegal posters are appearing (political, commercial, event-based)?
Angle: inadequate Sanitation enforcement or response capacity in this district?

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK versus 1.0 per week average over 8 weeks—a 400% spike (z-score: 4.0)—potentially signaling unsanitary conditions, pest issues, or animal welfare problems emerging in the neighborhood.
evidence: 5 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.0)
Represents acute shift in current week
Consistent with broader UNSANITARY CONDITION complaints (1,323 over 90 days, chronic issue)
reporting_angles: What is causing the spike: rodent infestation, wildlife distress, lack of collection service?
Interview NYPD Animal Care & Control and Sanitation about response protocols

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Tree/Branch Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK versus 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—pointing to deferred Parks maintenance or storm damage in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 3 overgrown tree/branch complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.42)
Community Board has standing request for 'Reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' (repeated year after year)
Aligns with chronic infrastructure underinvestment in district
reporting_angles: Site survey: which parks and streets have visible overgrown branches creating safety hazards?
Interview Parks Department on maintenance backlog and response time in CD112

themes_detail.label: Encampment Increase
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints rose to 23 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 4.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 411% spike (z-score: 4.3)—reflecting a possible wave of unsheltered populations or concentrated homeless encampments in the district.
evidence: 23 encampment complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 4.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.3)
Community Board has standing budget request for 'Enhance park safety through more security staff' (chronic concern)
Correlates with UNSANITARY CONDITION complaints (1,323 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Profile encampment locations and size: where are they concentrated? Any visible expansion?
Interview homeless outreach teams, NYPD, NYC Department of Social Services on resources and response capacity

themes_detail.label: Building/Use Violations Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Building/use violation complaints reached 13 THREE WEEKS AGO versus 6.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 108% spike (z-score: 4.32)—suggesting possible illegal conversions, overcrowding, or lack of compliance enforcement in residential buildings.
evidence: 13 building/use complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 6.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.32)
DOB filings show 399 total permits filed (351 alterations), suggesting active construction/conversion activity
District has 23 new building filings in last 90 days—possible connections to use violations
reporting_angles: Review DOB violation database: what specific building/use violations are being cited in CD112?
Interview Department of Buildings and housing advocates on enforcement gaps and illegal conversion patterns
